items.summary: Hurricane Simon reached Category 4 with 145 mph (230 kph) winds on Sunday, Oct 11, sitting about 65 miles WNW of Manzanillo with a hurricane warning in effect along Mexico's west-central coast. President Claudia Sheinbaum urged residents of Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacán to shelter indoors; evacuations were ongoing. Mexico's civil protection agency placed 28 municipalities in Jalisco and Colima at the highest cyclone alert level and 93 more at high alert. Puerto Vallarta's international airport temporarily closed Sunday; Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities.
items.title: Oct 11: Hurricane Simon at Category 4 (145 mph) nears Mexico's west-central coast; evacuations and warnings

items.summary: As of the 06:00 UTC Monday advisory, Simon had weakened to Category 3 with 115 mph (185 km/h) winds, centered near 19.9N 106.2W — about 140 miles WNW of Manzanillo and 45 miles SW of Cabo Corrientes — moving NW at 5 mph; whether the center would cross inland or stay just offshore was still uncertain. NHC forecast an additional 2-4 inches (5-10 cm) of rain through early Thursday, locally up to 8 inches, with isolated storm totals reaching 30 inches (76 cm) over Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco — life-threatening flooding and mudslides in steep terrain. No Mexico casualties or damage reports had surfaced as of Monday morning.
items.title: Oct 12: Simon weakens to Category 3 (115 mph) off Mexico; isolated 30-inch rain totals forecast

items.summary: Hurricane Isaias formed as Tropical Depression Nine in the Gulf on Oct 6, was named Oct 7, and became the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season on Oct 8 (80 mph) — one of the latest first hurricanes in Atlantic history (record: Oct 8, 1905). It peaked at Category 3 with 120 mph winds on Oct 9, then made landfall near Destin, Florida around 8:30 PM CT Friday, Oct 9 as a Category 2 with 105 mph winds. It was downgraded by 4 a.m. CT Saturday and became post-tropical over Alabama later Oct 10.
items.title: Oct 9: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall near Destin, FL as Category 2 (105 mph) after peaking at Cat 3

items.summary: Four deaths are confirmed: 2 in Escambia County, Florida and 2 in Alabama (Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey confirmed the two Alabama deaths Oct 10) — three killed by falling trees and one by generator carbon-monoxide poisoning, per NPR on Oct 12. Peak power outages reached roughly 940,000 customer accounts (over 1 million at one point per FoxWeather). As of Monday morning Oct 12, about 30% of Florida Panhandle customers were still without power (down from the peak), under 1% in Alabama; about 428,000 were still out in Florida at the last FoxWeather update (Oct 11). Pensacola was under a boil-water notice (Emerald Coast Utilities Authority).
items.title: Isaias toll: 4 dead; ~940k peak outages, ~30% of Panhandle still out Monday morning

items.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties on Oct 8; Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey declared for 40 counties. Mandatory evacuations of coastal Okaloosa County, Florida began at noon Thursday Oct 8; three Okaloosa airports closed Thursday evening; an evacuation notice went out for the western portion of Dauphin Island, Alabama.
items.title: Oct 8: states of emergency in 25 FL and 40 AL counties; coastal evacuations and airport closures

items.source_name: WNCY (BSEE data via Earth Science Associates)
items.summary: Pre-landfall on Oct 8, personnel were evacuated from 121 Gulf production platforms and 5 non-dynamic rigs; 63% of Gulf oil production (1.3 million bpd) and 57% of natural gas production (1.1 Bcf/d) were shut in, with roughly 9 million barrels of oil potentially lost over the storm's duration. The most exposed operators: BP, Chevron, ENI, Murphy Oil and Shell.
items.title: Oct 8: 63% of Gulf oil output (1.3M bpd) shut in; 121 platforms evacuated ahead of Isaias

items.summary: Isaias's inland remnants spawned confirmed tornadoes: the NWS confirmed an EF0 near East Arcadia, Bladen County, NC (~12:54 PM EDT Oct 11, 1.68-mile path, 75 mph peak, no injuries), three tornadoes in Georgia on Oct 10 (EF0 near Captolo and an EF1 at 105 mph near Newington), and a small tornado in Wallace, NC on Oct 11 that damaged a church and power lines with no injuries. Western North Carolina saw flooding plus an 840,000-gallon sewage spill into Hunting Creek, Burke County on Oct 11. NC Gov. Josh Stein said Monday that no one was reported hurt in the weekend storms. Separately, remnants of Pacific storm Rachel brought heavy rain and dangerous surf to Southern California (homes damaged in Long Beach, Newport Beach streets flooded) and one of Las Vegas's wettest October days.
items.title: Oct 10-11: Isaias remnants spawn tornadoes in NC and GA; 840k-gallon NC sewage spill; Rachel floods SoCal

items.summary: The NHC's 8 a.m. EDT Monday tropical weather outlook showed no active tropical cyclones in the Atlantic basin. One disturbance — an elongated low a few hundred miles west of the Cabo Verde Islands — carries a low 20% formation chance through both 48 hours and 7 days, with heavy rain and flooding risk for the western Cabo Verde Islands. NHC was also monitoring two tropical waves; the next Atlantic name would be Josephine.
items.title: Oct 12: no active Atlantic cyclones; one Cabo Verde disturbance at 20% formation chance

items.event_time_ist: 8 a.m. MDT advisory, Oct 12 (1400 GMT); CNN update ~12:30 PM PDT, Oct 12
items.summary: Hurricane Simon continued weakening Monday: CNN (~12:30 PM PDT) reports 105 mph per the latest NHC update; the 8 a.m. MDT NHC advisory had 110 mph with the center ~55 mi west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, moving northwest at just 3 mph. CNN reports landfall now expected sometime Thursday with winds near 100 mph; an AccuWeather expert says Simon could ultimately stall and never make a true landfall as an organized storm. The hurricane warning (Playa Perula to El Roblito plus Las Islas Marias) remains in effect.
items.title: Hurricane Simon downgraded to Category 2 as it crawls off Mexico's Pacific coast

items.event_time_ist: Announced at a news conference, Oct 12
items.summary: First reported Mexico casualty from Simon: an elderly person died in the southwestern state of Guerrero, according to Mexico's national Civil Protection coordinator during a news conference with President Claudia Sheinbaum. Sheinbaum described overall damage from Simon as 'minor,' saying Guerrero saw the most damage though less than expected, with some damage in Colima; she noted that Tropical Storm Rachel's impacts in Baja California were greater.
items.title: First reported Mexico death from Simon: elderly person in Guerrero

items.event_time_ist: Closures in effect since 6 p.m. local time, Oct 10
items.summary: Both of Mexico's main Pacific tourist airports are shut: Puerto Vallarta International will stay closed until 8 a.m. local time Tuesday, Oct 13 (extended, per Pacific Airport Group), and Manzanillo's airport has suspended all commercial flights — airlines canceled every scheduled flight over the storm threat, per GAP aviation notices. Both airports stopped operating at 6 p.m. local time Oct 10. Mexico's navy has also closed navigation at ports including Puerto Vallarta and Manzanillo.
items.title: Manzanillo airport flights suspended; Puerto Vallarta closure extended to Tuesday morning

items.summary: Simon's slow crawl brought flooding to Manzanillo, Mexico's largest Pacific port: heavy rain flooded homes and streets overnight into Sunday, with soldiers and the National Guard deployed to assist families — residents in the Alameda neighborhood waded through shin-deep water while troops bucketed water from homes. Mexico's civil protection agency kept 28 municipalities in Jalisco and Colima at its highest cyclone alert level and another 93 at high alert.
items.title: Heavy rain floods homes and streets in Manzanillo; soldiers assist residents

items.summary: Simon's remnant moisture is headed for the U.S.: the Weather Prediction Center has outlined an excessive-rainfall risk across parts of the Southern High Plains and Southwest Texas on Wednesday, Oct 14, with 1-2 inches of rain and isolated totals over 3 inches; NWS offices in Lubbock and Amarillo note heavy-rain potential even after the system dissipates. A slight risk of excessive rainfall extends from New Mexico and Texas to Missouri, and a cold front interacting with the remnants brings a Level 2-out-of-5 severe weather threat (hail, tornadoes) to the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles on Tuesday.
items.title: Simon's remnant moisture to fuel heavy rain and flooding across Texas and the Plains midweek

items.source_name: Newsmax / Pensacola News Journal / USA Today
items.summary: Recovery is advancing in Isaias's landfall zone: Destin Mayor Bobby Wagner told Newsmax Monday that ~80% of power is restored in Destin with 100% of water service back, and streets should be cleared of debris today. Florida Power & Light says most affected customers should have power by end of day Monday, Oct 12, with the hardest-hit parts of Escambia and Santa Rosa counties back online Tuesday, Oct 13. In Alabama, ~20,000 homes and businesses remain without power, but Alabama Power says 95% of affected customers are restored.
items.title: Isaias recovery: Destin at ~80% power and 100% water; most FL customers back by Monday night

items.event_time_ist: depression expected within 2 days of NHC outlook issued 11:00 AM PDT, Oct 12 (11:30 PM IST, Oct 12)
items.source_name: NHC Tropical Weather Outlook (via El Dorado Weather)
items.summary: NHC's Tropical Weather Outlook (11 AM PDT, Oct 12) raised the broad low-pressure system (EP93) several hundred miles south-southwest of Guatemala to a 90% formation chance through both 48 hours and 7 days (up from 80%/90% at 5 AM PDT). A tropical depression is expected to form well south of southern Mexico in the next two days while the system moves west-northwestward at around 10 mph. A 1009 mb low has formed near 08N93W with a large area of showers and thunderstorms.
items.title: New tropical depression expected to form south of southern Mexico (EP93)

items.event_time_ist: NHC Advisory 21 issued 8:00 AM PDT (8:30 PM IST), Oct 12
items.source_name: NHC Hurricane Simon Public Advisory (via Ventusky)
items.summary: NHC Advisory 21 kept Simon at 110 mph (Cat 2), ~55 mi WSW of Cabo Corrientes crawling NW at 3 mph, and Mexico downgraded coastal warnings: hurricane warning lowered to hurricane watch from north of Cabo Corrientes to El Roblito, and hurricane warning lowered to tropical storm warning from Playa Perula north to Cabo Corrientes. Remaining: hurricane warning for Las Islas Marias only; hurricane watch north of Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya; tropical storm warning Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes. NHC's 16:05 UTC discussion forecasts a northeastward turn and movement inland across Sinaloa on Thursday, with additional 2-4 inches of rain (isolated 8 inches) over Colima, Jalisco, Nayarit and Sinaloa through early Thursday and isolated storm totals up to 30 inches possible over Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco — life-threatening flooding and mudslides.
items.title: Simon: coastal warnings downgraded; landfall now expected Thursday in Sinaloa

items.summary: As of Monday morning, Oct 12, about 146,000 structures had no power in Florida (concentrated in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties) and around 20,000 in Alabama, per PowerOutage.us trackers — down from a ~950,000-customer peak (Edison Electric Institute). FPL, the hardest-hit utility (435,000 outages), now expects 85% restoration by end of Monday — a downward revision of its initial 95% estimate — with hardest-hit Escambia/Santa Rosa areas back online Tuesday, Oct 13. Alabama Power says 95% of affected customers are restored, with longer work in heavily damaged areas. Pensacola's boil-water notice remains in effect.
items.title: Isaias recovery: ~146k still without power in Florida, ~20k in Alabama; FPL trims Monday estimate

items.summary: The U.S. Department of Energy authorized an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve on Oct 10 — up to 2 million barrels each for ExxonMobil and BP America to keep refineries running, to be returned in 2027 with premium barrels. By Friday afternoon, about 71.5% of daily Gulf oil production (~1.46 million bpd) and 58.8% of natural gas were shut in, with 100+ platforms evacuated and 8 rigs evacuated or moved.
items.title: DOE authorized 4M-barrel SPR emergency exchange after Isaias shut in Gulf production

items.event_time_ist: NHC Advisory 22 issued 2:00 PM PDT (2:30 AM IST, Oct 13), Oct 12
items.summary: NHC Advisory 22 (2 PM MST Oct 12) lowered Simon's maximum sustained winds to 100 mph (still Category 2), centered about 75 miles W of Cabo Corrientes and about 210 miles S of Mazatlan, moving west-northwest at 3 mph with a minimum central pressure of 969 mb. Mexico discontinued the Tropical Storm Warning from Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes; a hurricane warning remains in effect only for Las Islas Marias, with a hurricane watch from Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya. Forecast: near Las Islas Marias tonight into Tuesday, then approaching the west-central Mexico coast Wednesday into Thursday; NHC says Simon could re-intensify somewhat by Wednesday and remain a hurricane through midweek, with rapid weakening after it moves inland late in the week. Rainfall: 5-10 inches across coastal west-central Mexico with isolated maximums of 15 inches over Sinaloa by Thursday; a dangerous storm surge is possible along the immediate coast near Las Islas Marias.
items.title: Simon down to 100 mph in NHC Advisory 22; coastal warnings trimmed again

items.event_time_ist: Jalisco civil protection briefing held morning of Oct 12 (aired ~11:15 AM PDT / 11:45 PM IST, Oct 12)
items.source_name: Jalisco civil protection briefing (via Jalisco Noticias)
items.summary: Jalisco's civil protection briefing Monday outlined the Simon response so far: roughly 14,000 people evacuated, about 8,500 tourists kept safely in hotels, and just over 800 people remaining in shelters. Starting Tuesday, Oct 13, non-essential preventive measures are being lifted: in-person school classes resume and tourism and private-supply businesses can gradually reopen stores and shopping centers; public transit is resuming, though government administrative offices stay closed pending infrastructure evaluations. Officials reported significant storm-surge damage in Cihuatlan and La Huerta, a river overflow affecting Colima, and a pending agricultural-damage assessment in Tomatlan; no wind damage was reported, though 3-4 meter swells are still expected through Wednesday. Azteca ADN40 field reports separately put Puerto Vallarta/Nayarit affected homes above 3,000.
items.title: Jalisco briefing: ~14,000 evacuated, schools resume Tuesday Oct 13; storm surge damage in Cihuatlan/La Huerta
Gulf of Mexico oil/gas shut-ins drop to ~30% as crews return
items.summary: US Gulf of Mexico producers had shut in 29.63% of current daily oil production and 24.81% of natural gas production as of 11:00 a.m. CDT Monday Oct 12, per the Marine Minerals Administration - a sharp recovery from Friday's 71.5% oil / 58.8% gas peak ahead of Isaias's landfall. Personnel remain evacuated from only 5 of 371 manned platforms and 1 of 11 fixed rigs as operators inspect facilities and restart output.

items.title: Landslide destroys house in Acapulco amid Simon's heavy rains
items.summary: Heavy rains ahead of Hurricane Simon triggered a landslide in Acapulco, Guerrero that destroyed a house, per AFP. The damage occurred as Simon's outer rainbands soaked Mexico's Pacific coast over the weekend. It is separate from the previously reported Guerrero storm death (an elderly person).

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (early-morning PDT report; flooding overnight Oct 11-12)
items.summary: Reuters on-the-ground reporting Oct 12: rising water levels in the Marabasco River in Cihuatlan, Jalisco (near the Colima border) prompted patrols by the Mexican Army, Civil Protection officials and the Red Cross; floodwater inundated streets and low-lying areas of the town overnight and riverside communities were placed on alert for possible evacuations. In the port city of Manzanillo, Colima, residents waded through flooded homes and streets as navy personnel helped remove water - resident Maria Elena Vazquez said 'Everything got flooded,' with water at ankle level inside homes. Corroborated by Rapid Times NGR (same wire reporting) and Virgin Radio Dubai/AFP (Sunday flooding in Manzanillo). Separately, Fox Weather projects Simon could make landfall near Mazatlan on Wednesday night, earlier than the NHC's Thursday Sinaloa window - a single-outlet forecast, not an official call.
items.title: Simon flooding: Marabasco River rising prompts Army/Red Cross patrols in Cihuatlan; riverside communities on evacuation alert
